correctness.rationale: The revised statement keeps the valid Littlestone results. The forest criterion follows by extension along a topological order; any shattered tree has distinct witnesses at distinct leaves. For a cycle the count 2^r−2 rules out depth r. Product additivity follows by concatenating trees and, for the reverse inequality, running separate optimal mistake-bound predictors. I generated orientations from all 120 vertex orders, independently obtained 46 distinct concepts, then replayed the frozen certificate by filtering the feasible concepts at each branch and confirmed all 32 witnesses. Exact tree-feasibility and VC-trace checks found the gap only for the full edge mask among all 64 subgraphs of the 2+3 template; the remaining 1+4 and smaller cases are covered by the pseudoforest proof. The bridge endpoints in each interior block are distinct degree-two vertices; bridges preserve planarity, can be made bipartite by alternating sides, and make an independent product. This gives exactly 6s−1 versus 5s−1.
residual_risks: Finite certificate replay establishes the six-edge base, not an arbitrary-graph Littlestone formula. No machine-formal proof is asserted.

originality.rationale: The original broad novelty framing did not credit equivalent prior coverage of its forest shattering criterion and uniform VC formula. It does not pass for that component: Kozma–Moran expressly prove both. The replacement makes those results prior background and confines the contribution to the Littlestone gap, its finite certificate/minimality and its exact connected planar subcubic amplification. It explicitly credits overlapping generalizations indexed later; neither establishes earlier provenance nor states the connected bridge-chain result. Best-of-knowledge pass for the revised contribution, not a priority claim for the VC result or for generic additivity.
residual_risks: Search and statement comparison are bounded; earlier graph-specific online-prediction work may exist. Later index dates do not establish historical priority, and the later claims were compared for overlap rather than independently proved.

checked_sources: Replacement RESULT.md theorem, minimality proof and bridge-chain construction
Frozen certificate.json; Kozma–Moran Proposition 15(i); Pikhurko definition of the different query objective
value.rationale: The five-vertex obstruction gives a genuine sharp boundary within bipartite graphs: the first two-cycle bipartite structure already admits adaptive shattering beyond forest rank. The graph family shows the gap is unbounded despite connectedness, planarity, bipartiteness and degree three, rather than merely under disjoint repetition. These are informative constraints on a natural orientation class; the revised work does not rely on the known VC formula for its contribution.
residual_risks: The amplifier proves no optimum over all subcubic graphs and leaves the two-edge-connected case open.
